one_month_reasoning: Eaton's Q3 2026 report (Nov 3) falls just OUTSIDE the window ending Oct 30, so no company print lands inside it. Events inside the window: FOMC Oct 27-28, where Polymarket (Sep 26) priced a 67% chance of a further 25bp hike after the Sep 16 hike, with the 10-year near 5.2%; a hike is largely priced, but a hawkish surprise hurts long-duration multiples like ETN's ~28x. Also late-October hyperscaler earnings (Microsoft/Alphabet/Meta/Amazon), whose 2027 capex commentary is the main short-term driver for data-center power names; sell-side already expects ~50%+ capex growth in 2027, so the bar is high. Pre-earnings drift after a guidance raise and September's +7.7% momentum are small positives, offset by rate risk. Net: about symmetric, median ~$433, lognormal at monthly vol 0.11 (39%/3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (NTM EPS at Sep 2027 of ~$16.8 for Eaton ex-Mobility x 26x = $437, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (NTM FCF/share ~$16.0 at a 3.6% yield = $444, weight 0.4). This is on the post-separation share: ETN holders also get Dana-combination shares worth roughly $13/share, which leave the ETN price when the deal closes in Q1 2027.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS (Q4'27-Q3'28) ex-Mobility $16.8 x 26x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027 consensus ~$15.7 grown ~13% (management's 12%+ EPS CAGR target through 2030, backlog up 33-103%) for a Q4'27-Q3'28 window gives ~$17.6; minus ~$0.8/share of Mobility earnings (Q2 sales $841M at 13% margin, about $0.43B/yr of operating profit after tax over ~390M shares) that leaves in the Dana RMT, partly offset by paying down debt with the $1.1B cash distribution.

10-year median TTM P/E ~26.6x (range 10.8-41.7x); today's forward ~28-30x. Cut toward the long-run median because the 10-year yield is ~5.2% with further Fed hikes priced, and AI capex growth is expected to slow sharply in 2028. Kept above the historical ~20x mid-cycle multiple because the business mix is now more electrical, data-center and aerospace, a mix the market prices at a premium (Vertiv ~49x).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF/share ~$16.0 (95-100% conversion of ~$16.8 EPS) / 3.6% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: $16.8 EPS x 95% conversion (the low end, because working capital builds with a backlog growing 33%+ and YTD FCF of $874M is back-half weighted)
Equivalent to ~27-28x FCF, consistent with the 26x P/E choice; the spread over the 5.2% 10-year is justified by 12%+ EPS growth
Context for leverage risk; not used directly in the per-share value

bear.story: By mid-2027 the market prices 2028 AI capex growth slowing to single digits (UBS sees 6%). Orders roll over from the +41% pace, rates stay above 5%, and the multiple falls to ~19-20x on ~$15 EPS. This repeats the DeepSeek/tariff drawdown of Jan-Apr 2025 (-38% from high to low) and the Jul-Dec 2025 slide (-22%).

base.story: Eaton delivers ~12-13% EPS growth, completes the Mobility RMT in Q1 2027 (price drops ~$13 when the Dana shares are distributed), and Boyd integrates. The multiple drifts down to ~26x while the backlog converts.

bull.story: Hyperscaler capex beats the $1.2T 2027 forecasts, margins move toward the 28% target early, and the multiple holds at ~32x on ~$18 EPS as the market re-rates Eaton toward the Vertiv/Schneider premium.

thesis_break_reason: About 26% below spot and near the Dec 2025 low of $312. At $320, ETN trades at ~19x its ~$16.8 NTM EPS, which only makes sense if the market expects earnings to fall: data-center orders cancelled or pushed out, Boyd margins breaking, or a recession (Polymarket 35% / Kalshi 24% by end-2027). A normal multiple swing with rates at 5%+ would not take it that low.

reasoning: Anchor: ETN's own 12-month returns since 2011 (145 monthly windows, Twelve Data) have a median of +14%, 5th-95th percentile of -15% to +69%, and are negative 32% of the time. That sample comes from a 15-year re-rating from ~12x to ~30x, so it is biased upward and I did not use its median. Long-run monthly vol is 24-28%, recent realized vol 39%, and drawdowns of 22-38% happened twice in 2025 alone. Valuation: at ~28-30x forward the stock sits near its 10-year high multiple (41.7x TTM high, ~26.6x median), while 10-year yields at 5.2% and priced Fed hikes argue for slow multiple compression. Fundamentals are strong: Q2 organic growth +14%, FY26 EPS guide raised to $13.50, Americas orders +41%, backlog up 33-103%, 2027 consensus ~$15.7. Fair value ~$440 on the post-Mobility share is about flat versus spot. The Q1 2027 Dana RMT distribution (~$13/share) mechanically lowers the unadjusted 2027-09-30 price, which is why the median sits slightly below spot (~$427). The distribution mixes 80% lognormal (median $445, sigma 0.30) with 20% bear regime (median $340, sigma 0.35, for a 2028 capex-cliff or recession re-rating). That gives an effective vol of ~35%, a fatter left tail, and a scenario mean of ~$440. Research was limited: Twelve Data estimates and targets were paywalled, and one Polymarket page returned 403, so its figure comes from the search snippet.
